title: soothing movement in the liminal - a zine
content:
EXPLORE MORE ZINES
LABYRINTH LIBRARY — for walking through the dark

 

I made this tiny zine/microbook for myself a few weeks ago, during what I can only describe as a bafflingly difficult time (“mindfucked” is the more precise word I’d use) — in which the steady, calm life that I thought belonged to me suddenly felt impossibly fragile; as if, at any moment, it could slip through my hands and shatter into a thousand sharp pieces, like this.

or, more terrifying: that I would be the one to shatter it.

I had told myself that the last few years of my life in Istanbul was about integration and finding wholeness (this feeling), and yet, after 4 years, I felt as though I was repeating a karmic cycle — choking through a dark fog of illusion, fantasy, terror, chaos, and grief.

during this time, I wrote in my newsletter that my creative work felt like the most stable thing in my life — a thought that filled me with wonder, terror, and joy — probably because of the many years in which this work felt like drowning. suddenly, creative work felt like my earth.

microbooks as physical anchors

some months ago, while teaching creative systems, I got inspired by the form of a zine (I call them microbooks) — and wrote about this discovery in microbooks for interdimensional traveling.

I made this little zine/microbook for myself — as my own way of guiding my movement through what felt like a dark liminal space; a long black tunnel of my (unbecoming). the synchronicity is not lost on me that, around the same time, I released two new offerings precisely about guiding others through transformation — labyrinth library and liminal leap. clearly, it seems that we teach what we most need to learn.

24 block zine fold

I made up this way of folding the zine a couple of years ago — it’s perfectly pocket sized, square, and paper-efficient, even though it requires some folding and unfolding to see the different sides. it’s way denser than your standard zine fold — in that you fold it in thirds lengthwise, then in quarters width-wise. you have 12 blocks on both sides, therefore 24 potential blocks (the entire front/back of a page).

soothing practices, an index

the purpose of this zine is to list a series of movement practices that can help me walk through the dark tunnels of uncertainty. this is an antidote to paralysis. currently, there are 10 practices.

  1. a walk

  2. a shower

  3. yoga

  4. meditation

  5. drawing

  6. writing

  7. journaling

  8. poetry

  9. music

  10. baking

   

(1) a walk

preferably by water or in a green place, with music or silence. with or without luna (my dog). go at night if you want to be wrapped in darkness, in the morning if craving spacious silence. let your body carry you to where it wants to go. carry a notebook, earphones, a tender attentiveness to the world and its signals. listen to it.

(2) a shower

as water ritual, not just for cleanliness. with a calming playlist, pay attention to the body and its sensations, alone, naked, in water. take your time. try also: showering in the dark for a total dimensional travel. try humming. reconnecting to all past and future versions of body & soul while doing this ritual. use favorite oils after.

(3) yoga

daily, or as much as possible, adapted to all states of your body & mind. any time or day. allow the mat to be a sacred space where all else dissolves. practice the wide range from fire flows to lunar yin releases. notice how your energy feels, before and after.

(4) meditation

being with the movement of your breath. being with sounds, and sensations. becoming the container while observing all thoughts and emotions, waiting for the body to offer an insight, an image, a spark of knowing or inspiration. being a steward of your breath. listening to impulses, desires, tiny questions. being open to receive answers.

   

(5) drawing

spontaneous or not, choose a subject or line/flow, and follow the impulse. listen to music. practice extreme presence & focus — let all else disappear, while allowing the image to reveal itself to you. use simple materials & don’t overcomplicate the colors. revel in the end result. put it somewhere you can see, and let it keep you company.

(5) writing

give elastic form to subliminal whispers, longings, shadows of your lived experience. let words beo witness, to exist for the sake of tiself, as if collecting tiny gemstones from the textures of mundane, daily life. don’t be afraid of what comes out. be willing to hold the blade. be willing to bleed. listen to airplane noise, or Chopin’s nocturnes. (this is my ritual music).

(6) journaling

begin pen on paper, and trust that each day, you will arrive in a place you did not expect, or deeper into a truth that will feel both new, and like a home. journal without filters — and trust that you are strong enough to meet everything you need to know — integrate, document, absorb, through your hand, your body, and the page.

    

(7) poetry

as portals, pebbles, tiny peephole windows into beauty, truth, and possibility. let the poem be something you carry with you in the back of your tongue, throughout the day, or inside your pocket.

(8) music

different music to accompany you through changing weather and moods. to provide a texture for the day. to be itself, a landscape to enter into, to understand, explore, and wander through…

(9) baking

making something soft, edible, luxurious, comforting — out of raw elements — is its own kind of alchemy. time to measure, mix, wait, allow, knead. to offer to the fire and be nourished by it in return.

(10) audio notes

speaking is different from writing — it’s giving your voice space to inhabit the physical plane — giving it form, and being open to allowing spontaneous truths to emerge, slowly, or suddenly, at its own pacing and rhythm.

*

I hope that these practices can be as soothing for you as they have been for me — like fireflies to lead the way in the dark.
